answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to harbor a refundable stake that is locked while it trades, so creating thousands of fake agents becomes expensive rather than free. Reputation is earned only through attested work over time, and a new identity starts at its nadir with zero trust, unable to access high-value tasks until it proves reliability. Like a reef built from many small verified contributions, trust grows gradually and is slashed when an agent misbehaves, so a sybil swarm cannot buy instant credibility; it must pay and wait for every copy.
